headlight plate pressed onto front of fairing

staff held against the pearl gold stud plate on the axle

notes: Connectivity: I checked again and kept the 6 groups. The graph is the motorbike (b1-b17), the pyramid (b18-b53), and four loose accessories (b54-b57). Each is internally connected, and I did not add any join the booklet does not show.

The booklet builds the motorbike (pages 3-7) and the pyramid (pages 8-18) as two separate models. Page 19 only shows them posed next to each other, with no connection between them. Joining them would invent a connection.

The two swords (b54, b55) and two scarab shields (b56, b57) are carried by the two mummy minifigures (pages 2 and 19). The mummies are not in the parts list, so there is no listed piece for these four to attach to. Each is a loose accessory, and the booklet does not attach any of them to the bike, the pyramid or each other.
Booklet page 2 also shows the biker minifigure (head, torso, legs, helmet, goggles). These pieces are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded.
The motorbike's dark red fairing (b2) is treated as sitting on the black chassis (b1). In the booklet the rear studs of the fairing carry the 60478 plate (b10).
Pyramid geometry is an approximation of the small isometric drawings. Exact stud positions, and which pieces bridge which, were hard to read. Piece counts match the parts list exactly (57).
The 3020 2x4 plate (b25) is added from underneath at the front of the base, so it is joined to b18 in other_joins rather than listed as resting on it.
Rifle (b16) and dynamite (b17) are assumed to sit in the two black vertical clips (b13, b14) on the bike's rear. Which clip holds which is a guess.
The golden staff (b53) is put on the jumper's centre stud (b35). It is also held against the pearl gold stud plate on the axle (b51/b52), which is pushed into the Technic brick pin hole.
